subsystems.name: Regolith handling
subsystems.role: gets loose surface material to the printer in a form it can use.
parts: magnetic separator to concentrate iron-bearing grains

subsystems.name: Deposition head
subsystems.role: delivers energy or binder to a thin layer of regolith.

subsystems.name: Motion platform
subsystems.role: positions the head accurately across the build area.
parts: rover-mounted variant for roads and berms

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: supplies kilowatts continuously and manages heat in vacuum.

subsystems.name: Binder and consumables
subsystems.role: supplies whatever the process needs beyond regolith itself.

subsystems.name: Structure and geometry design
subsystems.role: shapes the printed object so a brittle, weak-in-tension material still holds loads.
parts: blast berms and aprons for landing pads

subsystems.name: Autonomy and inspection
subsystems.role: runs construction with no crew on site.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the site
buildSteps.detail: Survey particle size, mineralogy and iron-rich grain content, because microwave and laser heating depend on how well the local regolith absorbs energy.

buildSteps.title: Excavate
buildSteps.detail: Robotic scrapers or excavators gather loose regolith from the top few tens of centimetres, avoiding sites where ice or other volatiles would be destroyed.

buildSteps.title: Beneficiate the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Screen out coarse rock, heat the material to drive off adsorbed gases and moisture, and optionally magnetically separate iron-bearing grains to improve energy absorption.

buildSteps.title: Lay the first layer
buildSteps.detail: The regolith is spread into a thin, even bed — millimetres to a few centimetres thick — inside a defined build zone or fed as paste to an extruder.

buildSteps.title: Fuse or bind
buildSteps.detail: A microwave, laser or concentrated-solar beam melts the grains into a solid, or a binder is jetted into the bed and cured, or regolith paste is extruded bead by bead.

buildSteps.title: Build up the shape
buildSteps.detail: The head or gantry indexes upward and repeats, layer over layer, printing arched or domed geometries that keep the brittle material mostly in compression.

buildSteps.title: Cool, cure and finish
buildSteps.detail: Printed sections are cooled slowly to avoid cracking; landing-pad surfaces are melted or glazed so rocket exhaust cannot scour them.

buildSteps.title: Verify and hand over
buildSteps.detail: Cameras and radar check layer bonding, and coupons printed alongside are tested for density and strength before the structure is used.

prerequisites.tech: In-situ resource utilisation (regolith excavation and processing)
prerequisites.why: sample-return and rover work has characterised regolith, but no mission has excavated and processed tonnes of it.
sintering and melting are energy-hungry, and nights and polar shadows demand storage or nuclear power.
printing must proceed for weeks with no crew, and lunar dust degrades mechanisms and optics.

prerequisites.tech: Sintering and binding behaviour in vacuum and low gravity
prerequisites.why: mostly limited to vacuum-chamber and parabolic-flight tests; melt pools and binder curing behave differently without an atmosphere.

pathway.milestone: vacuum-chamber, drop-tower and parabolic-flight demonstrations of sintering, melting and binder jetting; terrestrial analogue printing challenges
pathway.unlocks: evidence that regolith can be consolidated into structural shapes at all.

pathway.milestone: small payloads on the lunar surface that print and test bricks or pavers in real vacuum and low gravity
pathway.unlocks: data on dust, thermal cycling and process reliability outside a laboratory.

pathway.milestone: robotic construction of a landing pad apron and blast berms near a future base
pathway.unlocks: repeated landings without throwing high-speed grit at everything nearby.

pathway.milestone: printed shelters, roads and radiation shielding built by autonomous machines before crew arrive
pathway.unlocks: far less mass launched from Earth per unit of habitable volume.
